**6B.3 Research Note**

**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning no. Xi’s 2024 record includes real policies aimed at women, rural poor, low-income workers, and social security, but the strongest independent evidence still shows major marginalized groups facing repression rather than prioritization.

| Side | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Xi urges promotion of high-quality and sufficient employment | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-05-29 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202405/29/content_WS6657333ac6d0868f4e8e79f2.html) | Xi framed employment as a core mission and linked it to people-centered development, workers’ fulfillment, happiness, and security. | 6B.3, 6B.1, 6B.2 |
| Yes | China's No.1 central document for 2024 charts roadmap for rural revitalization | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-02-03 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/policies/latestreleases/202402/03/content_WS65be363cc6d0868f4e8e3c18.html) | The annual policy blueprint prioritizes food security, preventing relapse into poverty, rural industry, and income growth, which directly targets poor regions and vulnerable rural households. | 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.10 |
| Yes | Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Further Deepening Reform Comprehensively to Advance Chinese Modernization | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-07-21 | [page](https://www.mfa.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xw/zyxw/202407/t20240721_11457437.html) | The plenum resolution says improving quality of life, social fairness, and wellbeing are “ultimate objectives,” and explicitly prioritizes jobs, income distribution, social security, and public services. | 6B.3, 6B.1, 6B.2 |
| Yes | China creates 2.45 million jobs through work-relief programs | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-11-04 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/statistics/202411/04/content_WS672879d6c6d0868f4e8ec91e.html) | Local work-relief programs created 2.45 million jobs for low-income workers and paid 31 billion yuan in wages, showing concrete support for marginalized workers. | 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.9 |
| Yes | Beijing’s growth package included education, healthcare, social security, and environmental spending | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-03-25 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202403/25/content_WS6600afebc6d0868f4e8e569e.html) | The package promised more spending on education, healthcare, social security, and environmental protection, plus fairer treatment in tax relief and procurement. | 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.6 |
| Yes | Xi’s poverty-alleviation and farmers’ income push | english.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-12-18 | [page](https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202412/18/content_WS6762b5aac6d0868f4e8ee153.html) | Xi said policy should improve farmers’ income channels, consolidate poverty alleviation, and prevent large-scale relapse into poverty. | 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.10 |
| Yes | China’s property rescue package | Reuters | 2024-05-23 | [page](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/explainerchinas-latest-property-market-support-package--its-contents-and-whats-at-stake-3455636) | The package cut downpayments and mortgage floors, used SOE purchases of unsold homes, and financed project completion, which helps households and vulnerable homebuyers. | 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10 |
| Yes | Official H1 data said GDP grew 5.0%, employment and prices were generally stable | National Bureau of Statistics of China | 2024-07-15 | [page](https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/PressRelease/202407/t20240715_1955620.html) | Official midyear data show stable jobs, prices, and income growth, which supports a claim of at least partial preservation of living conditions for ordinary households. | 6B.3, 6B.2, 5B.9 |
| No | China: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report | Freedom House | 2024 | [page](https://freedomhouse.org/country/china/freedom-world/2024) | Freedom House says the CCP tightly controls state, media, online speech, business, and civil society, which means vulnerable groups were not being empowered through open protection of rights. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | World Report 2024: China | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | [page](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/china) | HRW says Xinjiang abuses amount to crimes against humanity, with mass detention and forced assimilation, showing a massive failure to prioritize Uyghurs and other minorities. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | China attempts to ‘gaslight’ international community at UN human rights review | Amnesty International | 2024-01-23 | [page](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/01/china-attempts-to-gaslight-international-community-at-un-human-rights-review/) | Amnesty says Beijing repackaged repression in Xinjiang and Hong Kong as stability, which looks like propaganda rather than real prioritization of vulnerable communities. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | China: Overseas students face harassment and surveillance in campaign of transnational repression | Amnesty International | 2024-05-13 | [page](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/china-overseas-students-face-harassment-and-surveillance-in-campaign-of-transnational-repression/) | Amnesty reports Chinese and Hong Kong students were photographed, followed, and pressured through family members, which is direct intimidation of a vulnerable group. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | Reuters on Hong Kong 47 convictions and detention | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | [page](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427) | Extensive pretrial detention, bail denial, and convictions show the state punishing political opposition rather than prioritizing marginalized political communities. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | Reuters on Article 23 in Hong Kong | Reuters | 2024-03-19 | [page](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxscope-of-hong-kongs-new-national-security-laws-3344082) | Article 23 broadened sabotage, sedition, and state-secrets offenses and raised life-imprisonment exposure, which weakens any claim of special protection for vulnerable groups. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | HRW on Xinjiang religious rules | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-31 | [page](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/31/china-religious-regulations-tighten-uyghurs) | HRW says the rules intensify “Sinicization,” threaten imprisonment for noncompliance, and sit inside a broader surveillance regime, which is coercive minority control. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |
| No | Reuters on RFA Hong Kong bureau closure | Reuters | 2024-03-29 | [page](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usfunded-radio-free-asia-shuts-hong-kong-bureau-citing-security-law-concerns-3358157) | Article 23 chilled independent reporting enough to force a bureau closure, which undermines support for marginalized voices and accountability. | 6B.3, 6B.1 |

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence on women, rural poor, low-income workers, and broad social-security rhetoric.
- I did not find strong 2024 independent evidence showing major improvement for children, elderly people, disabled people, or water/sanitation access specifically.
- For those groups, the record is thin, and the best evidence is official promise language rather than outcome data.
- So the strongest defensible reading is: some genuine prioritization of select vulnerable populations, but not a consistently broad or rights-based welfare-first commitment across marginalized communities.
